480	With your permission, a moment: let me take this whole topic
481	down to the personal level as well.
482	Sukkot is a festival of very, very great joy.
483	On Sukkot the greatest joy is mentioned, in the festival of Sukkot.
484	If we look at the verses of the Torah: on Pesach it is not written
485	"joy" at all; on Shavuot it is written once, and on Sukkot
486	it is written twice: "And you shall rejoice in your festival, you…"
487	"…for HaShem your Elokim will bless you…" "and you shall be altogether joyful."
488	"You shall rejoice in your festival, and you shall be altogether joyful."
489	Where does the great joy of Sukkot come from? There are
490	many angles on this, but one that I think is
491	very, very deep: what is the sukkah?
492	The sukkah is the point of trust in HaShem. The sukkah is
493	"the shade of faith." What is the shade of faith? It is
494	that you actually see — for this you must sit in a sukkah
495	that is under twenty cubits, so that you see the s'chach. Because
496	the s'chach is an expression of the Clouds of Glory. Sukkot corresponds to
497	the Clouds of Glory. What are the Clouds of Glory? The cloud of HaShem:
498	"And the pillar of cloud went and came between the camp of
499	Egypt and the camp of Israel," "and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet it lit up
500	the night, and the one did not come near the other all night." The clouds are
501	a fortress of protection: "He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High, in the shade of Shaddai shall lodge."
502	That is, the sukkah. "And there shall be a sukkah for shade by day,
503	for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and rain." The sukkah is protection, it is a fortress
504	of protection. What is the sukkah, really? It is a fortress,
505	it is a dwelling of…
506	Once, I remember, there was a war — Operation Protective Edge —
507	fire was coming from Gaza, it was years ago. So
508	someone called me and said: "Rabbi, they're shooting at us,
509	and we have nowhere…" I said to him: "What do you have?
510	Where can you take cover?" "We have nothing, the yard is open." I said
511	to him: "What do you have? A sukkah." I told him: go into the sukkah.
512	The sukkah is protection. If you have no other place there,
513	of course, if you have a safe room or something, that is better, rely on that and not
514	on the sukkah — we do not rely on a miracle. But if there is
515	nothing else, then go into the sukkah. The sukkah is a fortress
516	of protection. Now, what is the protection in the sukkah?
517	"So that your generations may know." When you know, when you live
518	with the awareness that the Holy One, blessed be He, leads us
519	and guides us, that in itself gives a person
520	divine protection. Trust in HaShem causes
521	a person to be protected. Right? So it is written: "And he who trusts
522	in HaShem, kindness surrounds him." And when I am filled with the awareness that HaShem,
523	blessed be He, runs the world and there is nothing besides Him, and I
524	am permeated with this awareness, this very thing draws down on
525	the person, as the Nefesh HaChaim writes, that it is a proven remedy
526	for a person to be silent in the depths of his heart, [knowing] that the Holy One, blessed be He,
527	runs the world and there is nothing besides Him, and this itself
528	will protect the person greatly. The holy Zohar says, Rabbi
529	Shimon bar Yochai writes: "Trust is strength
530	and might, and the Holy One, blessed be He…" that is, whoever places
531	his trust and his strength in the Holy One, blessed be He, is not afraid
532	of anything; all the people of the world — he is guarded and protected.
533	The power of trust in HaShem is an exceedingly great power. And where does it begin? From that great awareness:
534	"So that your generations may know." So when a person truly lives
535	with the awareness that HaShem, blessed be He, sees — how does King David
536	say it? "HaShem is my shepherd, I shall not lack." "I shall not lack, for HaShem
537	is with me." "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." "Even though I walk
538	through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil,
539	for You are with me." He does not live in some pastoral fantasy where
540	everything is always rosy. But "even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil,
541	for You are with me" — "You are with me" is not only meant
542	as if we are walking around here inside some tanks
543	and RPGs, and you go with the Holy One, blessed be He. There is
544	something deeper here. What it means is: I understand
545	that You, Master of the world, made this whole
546	reality, it is all great; I walk with You in everything,
547	because the whole world is an atmosphere of Divine presence. So King David walks, even in difficult moments,
548	with kindness, with justice, singing.
549	This trust in the Holy One, blessed be He, brings a person
550	to great joy. And then, once you have purified your heart
551	during those ten days of the deep work of the unity
552	of "there is nothing besides Him," so that when you reach Yom Kippur
553	you cry out "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom," in every
554	way, because it is no longer hidden, as if the kingship of HaShem were not revealed;
555	the kingship of HaShem is revealed and clear, that He is the one and only King.
556	When this shines within a person's heart, he is filled
557	with joy from this great faith of those ten
558	days. When I then go out into life on Sukkot —
559	this is an expression of going out into life — if I go out
560	into life with the Master of the world, I am joyful, because I
561	know, even if I am competing in a tender against someone,
562	I know that in the end no person touches what is prepared
563	for his fellow. I will make every effort on the visible level,
564	I will draw up professional sketches, I will work
565	well, bring a proper business plan, consult with
566	people who understand, I will bring, I will invest
567	at the level of trust, I will do everything that is needed, because
568	that is what the Holy One, blessed be He, wants from us, but I
569	will know in the depth of my heart that the Master of the world is directing
570	me, and I will arrive exactly at what is meant for me. I have
571	serenity. I am not attached to the result; I do all
572	the effort, and the result is in the hands of the Holy One, blessed be
573	He. "A horse is readied for the day of battle, but victory is HaShem's,"
574	says Rabbeinu Bachya in his introduction to Parashat Shelach Lecha.
575	"A horse is readied for the day of battle" — you must prepare
576	the horse, but you know that the Master of the world
577	determines what will be in the end: "victory is HaShem's." The same thing
578	Rabbeinu Yonah says: "Unless HaShem guards the city, the watchman
579	stays awake in vain."
580	…
581	From here one can infer that if HaShem guards the city, the watchman does not
582	stay awake in vain. That is, either way: if the watchman is
583	superfluous, it should have said: why do you guard at all?
584	HaShem guards the city, not you. But that is
585	not what is written. "Unless HaShem guards, the watchman stays awake
586	in vain," but if HaShem does guard, then the watchman does not stay awake in vain,
587	because how does His guarding appear? Through the soldiers, through
588	the guards.
589	We must make the effort, but we will not slide into the effort
590	in such a way that we build for ourselves a worldview as if this were the only thing that exists
591	here, and that's it, and everything depends on the boss, whether he accepts this,
592	and on my marketing, whether it succeeds in marketing
593	the products. No — I will do my part, but everything is in the hands of
594	Heaven, and this gives us serenity and trust and calm,
595	because "he who walks in integrity walks securely."
596	But in order for me to live a life of effort
597	out of a strong awareness of the existence of the Holy One, blessed be He,
598	I first of all need intensive days, which is…
